During these months of working with the relief employee, Jaime, we have observed two distinct patterns of behavior in the workplace, stemming from his bipolar mood fluctuations. On the positive side—accounting for 40% of the time—he acts as a competent employee who consistently applies his professional experience. On the negative side—the remaining 60%—his attitude toward work is somewhat concerning; this is attributed to personal and relationship issues, as well as a general lack of motivation or lethargy regarding his duties. These negative behaviors have led to various incidents, as he channels his stress and personal troubles in an aggressive manner—specifically when handling tools—without regard for the consequences, creating a risk that he could injure himself or those around him at any moment.
the unit stopped working mid job

Not to keep brining up the same thing. It's just gotten to a point where it's almost funny.
We sat in between runs 20 hours. Jaime is clearly having issues with his wife via the phone. We are not on the right floor 5 minutes and he's already calling her, after that he comes out amped up. We use a boom line to bring the tongs from the back of the draw works to the middle of the rig floor where we will then change from boom line to air hoist.

I ask all my guys and some roughnecks to put their hands on the tongs to hold back the swing as I don't want anyone to get hurt.

First he holds back with us then he decides this is taking too long and pushes hard ( while everyone else is still pulling back) we the sit the tongs on the floor, he quickly removes the boom winch and throws it behind him without saying a word or look what's behind him, a roughneck was standing there and luckily grabbed it, he gave me a look, all I can do is apologize to him as talking to jaime only has negative effects.

He mad a few more minutes issues during the run including basically throwing a hissy fit with the elevators and pin because the driller set slips, then came up a few inches so the elevators didn't sit on the handles as I mentioned before. Apparently it took too long for him and he showed his frustration.

Ryan Warren. It was his first job with us, I like how much he pays attention. He stopped jaime from opening the elevator doors on the 3rd joint because the clamp was pushing against the slip handle, and the slips were not fully set.

These are the kind of things I'm always looking out for but missed because it was on the opposite side from me, he not only noticed but spoke up, most new and or experienced hands wouldn't have even bothered to look or say anything.
